status_summary: On 2026-04-30 a House bill, H.R. 8628 (End U Visa Abuse Act), was introduced and referred to the Judiciary Committee; it would repeal the U nonimmigrant category but does not address T status, and the congress.gov action history lists no action after that referral. No bill to repeal T status and no rule, policy manual change or directive narrowing T or U eligibility was found. Parallel measures that do not change eligibility include ICE interim guidance 11005.4 (issued 2025-01-30 per a practice advisory) allowing civil enforcement against applicants and beneficiaries after legal consultation, which a federal district court stayed for three classes on 2026-05-20 (appeal filed 2026-06-19); a 2025-11-03 proposed rule changing how T adjustment applicants show good moral character; and a 2025-12-22 USCIS policy alert on confidentiality and prohibited-source information in VAWA, T and U cases.

timeline.event: ICE issued interim guidance 11005.4 (dated 2025-01-30 per a practice advisory; the memo itself bears no date), rescinding Directive 11005.3 and letting officers take civil enforcement action against current or potential beneficiaries of victim-based benefits after consulting legal counsel; it does not change T or U eligibility.
Immigration Center for Women and Children and others filed a class action in the Central District of California challenging the ICE guidance (No. 2:25-cv-09848).

DHS published a proposed rule on USCIS biometrics (RIN 1615-AC99) that would change how T nonimmigrants applying to adjust status demonstrate good moral character, including removing the presumption for applicants under 14; it does not change eligibility for T or U status itself.

USCIS issued policy alert PA-2025-34 on VAWA, T and U requests, citing suspected fraud and rapid growth in filings and changing how confidentiality protections and prohibited-source information are handled; per the report it does not change eligibility criteria.

H.R. 8628, the End U Visa Abuse Act, was introduced in the House with two cosponsors and referred to the Judiciary Committee; it would repeal INA section 101(a)(15)(U) and make conforming amendments, without addressing T status.
The court preliminarily certified three classes (pending petitions, deferred action, stay of removal) and stayed the 2025 guidance as to them, granting the injunction motion in part.
The government appealed to the Ninth Circuit (No. 26-3961).
